title: Visual and Patient related Outcomes After Implantation of the Clareon PanOptix IOL vs. AT ELANA IOL in Femtosecond Laser Assisted Cataract Surgery (PANAMA)
summary:
Das Ziel dieser Studie ist ein Vergleich des Visus in der Nähe, im Intermediärbereich und in der Ferne sowie der Vergleich von visuellen Beeinträchtigungen, Brillenunabhängigkeit und Patientenzufriedenheit nach Implantation von zwei diffraktiven trifokalen Intraokularlinsen (IOL) in Femtosekundenlaser gestützter Kataraktoperation (FLACS) bei Patienten mit altersbedingter Katarakt.
Hypothese: die Clareon PanOptix IOL (CNWTT0) erzielt einen besseren binokularen fernkorrigierten Intermediärvisus im Vergleich zur AT ELANA IOL (841P) in 60 cm und einen größeren Prozentsatz an Patienten, welche „überhaupt nicht“ für „Halos“ im McAlinden Fragebogen für störende Lichtempfindungen bei der 3-Monatskontrolle angeben.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Availability, willingness, and enough cognitive awareness to comply with examination procedures. 
2.	Bilateral age-related cataract 
3.	Patients suitable for bilateral implantation with either one of the trifocal IOLs with femtosecond laser assisted cataract surgery 
4.	Legally capabable to give informed consent and personally signed informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Age of patient <18 years 
2.	Irregular astigmatism and severe/moderate ocular surface disease
3.	Expected postoperative corneal cylinder >0.75 D via IOL Master 700  
4.	HOA measured by Pentacam exceeding 0.3 microns in standard display with 4mm pupil. 
5.	Difficulty for cooperation (distance from their home, general health condition) 
6.	Clinically significant glaucoma (subjects with repeat glaucomatous structural or functional pattern loss noted on VF or OCT) as well as subjects with IOP >21mmHg measured during screening visit or the current use of any glaucoma medications.
7.	Macular degeneration, macular edema, or proliferative diabetic retinopathy 
8.	Patients with corneal dystrophies  
9.	Any ocular comorbidity having a significant effect on the postoperative clinical outcomes 
10.	History of ocular trauma or prior ocular surgery including refractive procedures 
11.	Capsule or zonular abnormalities that may affect postoperative centration or tilt of the lens (e.g. pseudoexfoliation syndrome, chronic uveitis, Marfan’s syndrome)  
12.	Pupil abnormalities (non-reactive, tonic pupils, abnormally shaped pupils or pupils that do not dilate under mesopic/scotopic conditions)
